thread:
mira: Customer reported partial JSON from SSE stream; final chunk missing, finish_reason not present. Happens intermittently (about 1/20 requests).

mira: Repro steps they gave: simple curl to our /v1/stream endpoint, pipe to jq, sometimes jq errors out on EOF. Example they sent:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"{...}","stream":true}' | jq .
```

mira: They attached truncated dump: last bytes are `...
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}]}` then connection closed. No `data: [DONE]` or finish_reason.

alex: Are they behind a proxy or using a mobile client? Proxy timeouts + abrupt RST can drop final chunk. Any client reconnect headers present?

mira: They said it's from a Node worker behind CloudRun. Occurs after ~30s sometimes. No explicit resume headers set by client.

samir: Can we check ingress logs for that trace? Ask for x-rw-trace or request id. I can pull proxy timeouts.

mira: Sent trace header: x-rw-trace: rw-7d9b2f. Attached server-side last log lines:
```
2026-02-12T14:22:03.112Z INF stream.start trace=rw-7d9b2f model=rwd-3b
2026-02-12T14:22:04.987Z DBG chunk.emit trace=rw-7d9b2f token=... seq=1
2026-02-12T14:22:33.105Z DBG chunk.emit trace=rw-7d9b2f token=... seq=18
2026-02-12T14:22:33.106Z INF connection.close remote=198.51.100.12 reason=client_reset
```

samir: That `client_reset` at 33s looks like an abrupt close from the client side. If client's TCP FIN/RST landed before the final flush, our last buffer might not reach them. Looks like streaming kernel socket close before we wrote terminal frame.

emily: Could HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 matter? CloudRun typically uses HTTP/1.1 to our edge. We have a known edge case where keepalive/idle proxies send RST on long-lived streams > 30s. There's an open mitigation to send periodic padding events to keep proxies alive.

mira: Customer says padding didn't help previously; we asked them to enable client-level reconnect with resume token. They don't currently send resume headers; their client is naive.

alex: Short-term workaround: add explicit small heartbeat SSE event every 10s from our runtime to prevent proxy idle timeouts. Long-term: support resumable streams (sse-resume header and last-event-id style token).

samir: I can patch a runtime flag to emit `data: "\u200b"` heartbeats and also ensure final chunk is flushed with SO_LINGER set. Will test on staging.

mira: For the customer: requested they try curl with `--http1.1 --no-buffer` and set `--keepalive-time 10` on their side, or use our JS SDK which implements reconnect/resume. Suggested sample curl to repro check:
```bash
curl -v --http1.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --no-buffer https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"test","stream":true}'
```

mira: Customer replied they can reproduce with curl; will test our heartbeat build.

deploy-bot: Promotion to staging cluster scheduled: runtime/heartbeat-flag -> staging at 2026-02-12T16:10:00Z.

alex: Next steps: samir deploys heartbeat patch to staging, run 1k stream requests with simulated client resets and confirm terminal frame emitted or resume info persisted. If passes, promote to prod and notify customer.

mira: Noted — keeping ticket open, will update customer once staging results are in. :thumbsup:
